_comment: Failure modes, each traced to a specific issue. 'symptom' is quoted or closely paraphrased from the reporter; 'fix' is what the reporter or a maintainer actually did, or explicitly 'no fix reported'. evidence_level: 1 = reporter observation, 2 = maintainer confirmed, 3 = fixed in a named released version. No item here is inferred.
_why_this_section_exists: The model merged into llama.cpp on 2026-08-27. Every issue below is from a runtime that DOES support it. The failure modes are not about the model being unsupported; they are about the specific things that break. Anyone reading only the '180B on a 12GB card' headline will hit these.

failures.title: N-gram table reported as not resident on newer prebuilt binaries (cause unconfirmed)
failures.symptom: On builds newer than 10665 the reporter observed the model loading and generating correct output while prefill was extremely slow. Their hypothesis, explicitly unconfirmed, is that the ~51B-parameter N-gram embedding table (20M bigram+trigram entries near layer 2) is not resident, so per-token lookups hit host memory and mmap page faults instead of being prefetched.
failures.environment: Windows, dual RTX PRO 5000 with 160 GB DDR5, UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF, -c 262144
failures.root_cause_status: Reporter's hypothesis, explicitly unconfirmed. No maintainer statement found.
failures.fix: Closed. The reporter states the community prebuilt binary at build 10665 behaves correctly. No maintainer-confirmed root cause or fix version was found.
failures.practical_advice: If prefill is pathologically slow but output is correct, check build age before blaming the model or the quant.
failures.state_meaning: closed on GitHub; a closed issue is not the same as a released fix - see fix for the version if one is named
failures.output_observation: The reporter did not report wrong answers. Nothing errored; prefill was the only thing affected. We are not claiming the outputs are correct in general - only that this report did not describe an output problem.

failures.title: Host RAM grows ~12 GiB/hour of normal chat until swap-thrash
failures.symptom: On build b10909-mix-bea84f7 the llama-server process footprint grows continuously during ordinary multi-turn conversation, roughly +12 GiB per hour. On build b10830-mix-d5c17a0 it stays flat at ~2.1 GiB regardless of usage.

measurements.build_a_stable: VmRSS 2.1 GiB, VmSwap 0, flat across days
measurements.build_b_fresh: VmRSS 19.2 GiB, VmSwap 9.6 GiB, RSS+Swap 28.8 GiB
measurements.build_b_after_1h: VmRSS 26.1 GiB, VmSwap 14.7 GiB, RSS+Swap 40.8 GiB

failures.environment: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121a, 128 GB unified memory, aarch64), Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.142, unslothai portable builds, IQ2_XXS/Q2_K imatrix GGUF (86.7 GB, checkpoint 0731), --ctx 32000, DSpark speculative decoding enabled
failures.consequence: With ~70 GiB committed to the GPU pool the kernel spilled 15 GiB to swap and the host swap-thrashed under concurrent load, twice, requiring a reboot.
failures.fix: No fix reported. Open at time of writing. The practical mitigation is the older build.
failures.practical_advice: On unified-memory systems (such as the reporter's DGX Spark setup), process memory growth can lead to swap-thrash under load. The reporter recommends pinning to the known-stable build (b10830-mix-d5c17a0).
failures.fix_status: no fix reported; open at time of writing
failures.state_meaning: open at the time of writing
failures.severity_note: On the reporter's 128 GB unified-memory box this stopped being slow and became fatal - swap-thrash under load, twice, requiring a reboot. We are reporting that experience, not a general property of all such machines.

failures.title: RTX 50-series (sm_120): reported wrong answers with CUDA 13.2 on IQ1_S / IQ2_S / IQ3_S
failures.symptom: On Linux with CUDA 13.2 on an RTX 5070 Ti the engine loads and serves normally with no errors in the log, but every answer is wrong. 'What is 2+2?' returns '4+4=8.8.' Translating 'good morning' to German returns 'Good morning'. Most other prompts end after 1-2 tokens or loop.
failures.environment: RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB (sm_120), driver 580.178.04, Ubuntu 24.04, Core Ultra 7 265K (AVX2, no AVX-512), 62 GB RAM, Strata 6f32ec0 / engine 0.1.39

isolation_matrix.llama_cpp_3cf0325_cuda_13.2_gpu_offload_: garbage, 0/12 on a small task suite
isolation_matrix.llama_cpp_test_backend_ops_cuda_13.2: MUL_MAT 44 FAIL, MUL_MAT_ID 22 FAIL, only iq1_s, iq2_s, iq3_s affected (ERR 0.4-0.66)

failures.diagnosis: What the reporter established: the same build is correct with -ngl 0 (CPU only) and wrong with GPU offload, and test-backend-ops shows MUL_MAT 44 FAIL / MUL_MAT_ID 22 FAIL confined to iq1_s, iq2_s, iq3_s under CUDA 13.2. That localises the fault to the GPU path for those quant types. It does not establish the mechanism - a compiler bug, a kernel implementation bug and a driver interaction all remain consistent with the evidence, and no maintainer has ruled any of them out.
failures.fix: No fix reported. The reporter states CUDA 13.0 works on the same card.
failures.practical_advice: If answers are wrong rather than missing, and you are on an RTX 50-series card, check your nvcc version before anything else. This fails silently.
failures.fix_status: reporter-tested workaround, not a maintainer-confirmed fix
failures.evidence_level: 1 = reporter reproduction with an isolation matrix
failures.state_meaning: open at the time of writing

failures.title: Coder variant answers wrong or loops on Chinese and other CJK text
failures.symptom: With half the experts removed, Chinese answers came out wrong or looping where English was fine.
failures.mechanism: The Coder keeps 256 of each layer's 512 experts, chosen on code data. The drop is not language-neutral.
failures.fix: Use Q2_0, IQ2_XS or IQ3_S, which keep every expert, whenever you need CJK text.
failures.practical_advice: Do not pick the Coder for Chinese work even though it is the only published variant targeting 32 GB RAM setups.
failures.state_meaning: not a GitHub state; this is a documentation reference
failures.evidence_level: 2 = documented by the project in docs/MODELS.md, issue #438

failures.symptom: Strata's --vision cpu path caps images at 300 tokens while llama.cpp's Qwen-VL multimodal path requests at least 1024.
failures.fix: Closed in Strata. Relevant if you are comparing the two paths on image input.
failures.state_meaning: closed on GitHub; a closed issue is not the same as a released fix - see fix for the version if one is named

failures.title: Vision input on AMD: works on Linux through the CPU, unavailable on Windows
failures.symptom: Strata's README states AMD cards read pictures on Linux through the processor; on Windows they cannot yet.
failures.fix: No fix reported. Use text only, or an NVIDIA card for image input on Windows.
failures.state_meaning: closed on GitHub; the limitation is documented in Strata's README, which is the durable form
failures.evidence_level: 2 = documented by the project in its README

failures.title: Tool call written inside <think> without </think> is returned as reasoning_content
failures.symptom: A tool call emitted inside the think block without a closing tag is surfaced as reasoning_content rather than as a tool call, so agent harnesses lose it.
failures.practical_advice: Relevant if you are wiring this into a coding agent and tools appear to be ignored.

failures.note: The Swift 1.5 fine-tune exists specifically to shorten thinking, which is the project's own answer to this.

failures.note: The model itself supports 262,144 natively. This is an installer policy, not a model limit.

measured_throughput_caveat: System A rows are not all from the same engine build: Q2_0 was measured on engine 0.1.36, the rest on 0.1.26. So the spread across quant rows is a mix of quantization effect and engine-version effect and should not be read as a clean quantization comparison.
